message:
docs(release): 0.2.109 signed, and the server does not need restarting

The manifest is signed with the existing operational key -- no new key, and
.claude/rel/0.2.108 was neither read nor written.

Three implementations, because a signer agreeing with itself is not evidence: a
signature made with the wrong encoding self-verifies just as happily. Node's
update_manifest.js and OpenSSL via python-cryptography both accept the real
document and both refuse it with one byte moved; the C++ default_verifier()
accepts a fixture signed by the same key. That last one is written down as what
it is -- it proves the compiled-in key accepts this key's signatures, not that
the product read this document.

While writing the Node check I had Status.Ok, which does not exist. The
acceptance check failed and BOTH negative controls passed, because `!==
undefined` is true of anything. One wrong constant disabled two negative controls
at once, and without the acceptance check all three would have looked green.

The handoff answers the restart question with the code rather than a guess:
handleUpdateManifest reads the file on every request (server.js:425), so swapping
windows.manifest and windows.sig takes effect immediately. Only an env change
would need a restart, and this release changes no env.

Also recorded: HostAgent lives in GNLinkStream.exe, not GNLinkHost.exe. Looking
in the supervisor first nearly produced a "the fix is missing" report.
